name: OR-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Cliff Bentz running with a 15-to-1 fundraising advantage
No polling and no expert ratings; prediction markets price Bentz near 95%
Democratic challenger Chris Beck is minimally funded
model.rationale: This eastern Oregon seat is firmly Republican, Bentz is the incumbent with over $1.4 million on hand against Beck's $54,000, and markets give Democrats only about a 4% chance. With no polls or ratings to suggest movement, the race stays safely Republican.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing Beck within single digits, or major outside spending entering the race, would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oregon's second district covers the state's rural east and south and leans Republican by about fourteen points. Cliff Bentz, the incumbent, was renominated without difficulty and holds a large financial edge, with roughly $1.4 million on hand compared to about $54,000 for Democrat Chris Beck. No outside groups have reported spending in the race.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the picture rests on the district's lean, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets price Bentz's chances near 95%. All signs point to a comfortable Republican hold, with Beck needing an exceptional shift in the political environment to compete.
